sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp. Sec. 3.2 'Phuza phonology in brief', pp. 6-7 (datapoint Phuza-BJB, Bujibai village, Lengquan Township, Mengzi County).
sources.note: SILENT. The sketch gives the syllable template {(C)(G)V(V)T}, 44 onsets, rhymes, and 'Four contrastive lexical tonemes.. high-level /55/, mid-level /33/, low-rising /13/ and mid-falling /31/', non-contrastive tense voice on /13/, and tone sandhi (/55/>[45], /13+31/>[21-21], /31+31/>[31-21], /31+31+31/>[31-21-21]); the words stress, accent, prominence, unstressed occur nowhere in the 144-page file.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-106: create [ypz] Phuza (adopted 2008-01-14), with the New Code Request form. SIL International. 8 + 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Identity: 'Phuza appears to be most closely related to Phupa and Alugu phylogenetically, but RTT testing of Phuza on Alugu and of Phupa on Phuza both point to low levels of intelligibility.. Phuza shares 71% lexical similarity in core vocabulary with Phupa'; autonym Phuza; alt. Phu'a, Phujitsu, Hei Phu (Black), Phula; 6,000 speakers; SW Mengzi and SE Gejiu counties.

tone.says: P. 39, as subgrouping evidence for a Phupa-Phuza micro-clade: 'Phupa and Phuza. sources.note: Comparative study of pathways to rising tone values across 11 Ngwi (Loloish) clusters using reflexes of Proto-Ngwi tone categories (abstract: '*high > rising' found in nine clusters, some splits conditioned by prevocalic consonants). Phuza enters as a doculect with 692 tone-transcribed forms carrying four Chao values 55 / 33 / 13 / 31 (e.g. m31 tshɯ55 'sun', la33 ba33 'moon'), i.e. Pelkey's four-toneme system; whether the article discusses Phuza's low-rising /13/ individually is not established (full text not opened). No new first-hand Phuza data.
